chapterName: Early Republic: The Conflict of the Orders - Toward Resolution (450-367 BCE)

questions.question: Which former consul, roused by the geese, hurled the first Gallic attacker off the Capitoline?
questions.explanation: The honking geese of Juno woke Marcus Manlius, who threw the first attacker down the slope, saving the citadel.
questions.sourceQuote: Their noise roused Marcus Manlius, a former consul, who hurled the first attacker down the slope.

questions.question: According to Livy, where was Camillus living in exile before being recalled as dictator to fight the Gauls?
questions.explanation: Livy places Camillus in exile at Ardea, a town south of Rome. Yet the Greek historians Polybius and Diodorus Siculus never mention him.
questions.sourceQuote: According to Livy, Camillus was in exile at Ardea, a town south of Rome, and was recalled as dictator.

questions.question: When the Gauls demanded the Fabius brothers be handed over, what did Rome do?
options: Elected them consular tribunes for the next year
Put them on trial for murder
questions.explanation: Instead of surrendering the envoys who broke neutrality, Rome honoured them with election as consular tribunes. Enraged, the Gauls marched on Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: Instead, the Romans elected them consular tribunes for the next year.

questions.question: Why did the dictator Publius Manlius Capitolinus anger the patricians?
options: He refused to fight the Volscians
He handed the Sibylline Books to plebeians
He freed all debtors from prison
He picked a plebeian as his deputy
questions.explanation: Manlius Capitolinus chose a plebeian deputy, upsetting the patricians. Licinius and Sextius then won a tenth term, and their whole package went through.
questions.sourceQuote: A second dictator, Publius Manlius Capitolinus, angered patricians by picking a plebeian deputy.

questions.question: How did the Licinian laws change the guardianship of the Sibylline Books?
options: The books were moved to the temple of Juno at Veii
The priesthood was opened only to women
Ten priests replaced two, five of them plebeians
The Senate took over direct control
The books were handed to the tribunes
questions.explanation: Two patrician priests were replaced by ten, five of them plebeians. For the first time, the patricians' monopoly on priesthoods was broken.
questions.sourceQuote: The new law replaced them with ten priests, five of them plebeians.

questions.question: Between 444 and 401 BC, roughly how many of about a hundred consular tribunes were plebeians?
questions.explanation: Although Livy claimed the office was a concession open to plebeians, only two of about a hundred holders in this period were plebeians. Around 400 BC this changed.
questions.sourceQuote: Between 444 and 401 BC, only two of about a hundred consular tribunes were plebeians.

questions.question: Which elderly Roman struck a Gaul with his ivory staff, triggering the massacre in the city?
questions.explanation: A Gaul stroked Marcus Papirius's long beard, and Papirius struck him with his staff. The massacre began, and houses were plundered and burned.
questions.sourceQuote: Then one Gaul stroked the long beard of Marcus Papirius, who struck him with his ivory staff.

questions.question: How does Cornell's view of the sack differ from Livy's account of Rome being burned and hastily rebuilt?
options: He thinks the Romans burned the city themselves
He thinks the Gauls left most buildings standing and went home once paid
He thinks the Gauls never actually entered Rome
He thinks the city was rebuilt on an orderly grid
He thinks the Gauls occupied Rome for several decades
questions.explanation: Cornell believes the Gauls mainly wanted loot and left once paid. He also notes that haphazard street plans were common in ancient cities anyway.
questions.sourceQuote: In his view they left most buildings standing and went home once they were paid.

questions.question: What made Licinius and Sextius finally give way in 370 BC after blocking elections for years?
options: A revolt by the Fabius family
A new Gallic invasion from the north
An attack on Roman territory by Velitrae
An outbreak of plague in Rome
questions.explanation: They relented when Velitrae, a town of the Volscians, attacked Roman territory. Even so, the pair were re-elected year after year.
questions.sourceQuote: They gave way only in 370 BC, when Velitrae, a town of the Volscians, a people south-east of Rome, attacked Roman territory.

questions.question: Which of these were roles or powers of the new office of praetor? (select all that apply)
options: Vetoing business in the Plebeian Council
questions.explanation: The praetor was Rome's chief judge, presided over criminal trials and could command an army. The office was at first reserved for patricians.
questions.sourceQuote: The praetor served as Rome's chief judge, presiding over criminal trials.
